Anthropic shipped Claude Fable 5.1 on September 1, 2026, its first update since Fable 5 launched on June 9. The context window is the same 1 million tokens. Max output is the same 128,000 tokens. Base input and output pricing are the same $10 and $50 per million tokens. So what actually changed? Eight things, and they range from "notice it in your invoice next week" to "notice it in a lab that maps Venus."

This is the same underlying model released two ways. Claude Fable 5.1 is generally available with Anthropic's standard safeguards. Claude Mythos 5.1 is the restricted-access sibling, gated behind Anthropic's Cyber Verification Program (defensive security work) and Life Sciences Verification Program (the biology program, which Anthropic says was developed in partnership with the US government). We cover the model access split separately in how to access Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5; this post is about what's different in the 5.1 update itself, listed in the order a team already running Fable 5 in production is likely to feel them.
The 8 changes at a glance
Cache read pricing dropped 75%: from $1.00/MTok to $0.25/MTok, the single biggest lever if you run agentic workloads with repeated context.

Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 more than doubled: 24.7% to 52.6%, the largest single benchmark jump in the release. AutomationBench (17.1% to 31.4%) and Terminal-Bench 4.0 (42.0% to 55.8%) also rose by more than 13 points.
A new sibling model, Mythos 5.1: restricted access, and it beats Fable 5.1 on agentic coding.
Anthropic's own recommendation shifted: an Opus model, not Fable 5.1, is the default pick for most workloads. At launch that was Opus 5; since September 22, 2026 it is Opus 5.5.
Humanity's Last Exam (no tools) rose: 57.8% to 60.9%.
CursorBench 3.2.0 rose: 70.5% to 73.4%.
OSWorld 2.0 (partial) rose: 72.9% to 77.9%, a 5.0-point gain.
Named scientific and real-world results Anthropic cited at launch: protein design and GPU speedups (both from Mythos 5.1), Venus mapping, and one investment firm's root-cause debugging story.

Source for all benchmark and pricing numbers: Anthropic's launch announcement and the model overview docs. We've also added Fable 5.1 to our own AI model comparison hub if you want to see it stacked against every other current model on the same page.
1. Cache read pricing dropped 75%

Cache reads went from $1.00/MTok on Fable 5 to $0.25/MTok on Fable 5.1. Everything else on the price sheet held steady: input is still $10/MTok, output is still $50/MTok, batch API is still 50% off base rates. Cache writes are $12.50/MTok for the 5-minute tier and $20/MTok for the 1-hour tier.

Why this is #1 on the list: it's the only change on this page that hits your bill without you changing a single line of code. Anthropic states this brings typical-workload costs down about 25% and highly agentic workload costs down up to about 45% versus Fable 5 at identical base prices. That "up to 45%" number specifically targets teams running long agent loops with repeated context, exactly the workload we build for clients doing custom workflow automation. If your agent re-reads the same system prompt and tool definitions on every step, a 75% cut on cache reads compounds fast.

2. Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 more than doubled

24.7% to 52.6%. It is the biggest gain in Anthropic's comparison table. The next largest are AutomationBench (17.1% to 31.4%, +14.3 points) and Terminal-Bench 4.0 (42.0% to 55.8%, +13.8 points), each about half as big. Terminal-Bench-Science measures scientific computing and research-coding tasks in a terminal environment, and the jump lines up with the scientific use cases Anthropic highlighted at launch (more on those in #8).

Worth noting: Fable 5.1 still isn't the top scorer on every science-adjacent benchmark. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, the general agentic-coding test, Mythos 5.1 posted 60.9% against Fable 5.1's 55.8%. That gap is why item #3 exists.
3. Mythos 5.1 is a real sibling model, not a rebrand

Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 are the same underlying model with different safety filters. Fable 5.1 ships generally available with Anthropic's standard safeguards. Mythos 5.1 is restricted to organizations vetted through Anthropic's Cyber Verification Program (cybersecurity) or Life Sciences Verification Program, which Anthropic says was developed in partnership with the US government.

The reason to know this if you're not eligible for either program: Mythos 5.1 outscores Fable 5.1 on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (60.9% vs 55.8%). If you've read that Fable 5.1 "won" every benchmark Anthropic published, that's not quite right, its restricted sibling wins one of them. For most teams this is academic since Mythos access requires formal vetting, but if you're evaluating vendor claims, it's the kind of detail worth getting right.
4. Anthropic now points most workloads to Opus, not Fable 5.1

This is a positioning change, not a benchmark number, and it's easy to miss if you only skim the comparison table. When Fable 5.1 shipped, Anthropic's docs recommended Opus 5 for most workloads, reserving Fable 5.1 for "demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work, or when your evals on Claude Opus 5 at higher effort still fall short."

Update, September 26, 2026: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5 on September 22 at $4/$20 per million tokens, and its models overview now reads: "start with Claude Opus 5.5 for most workloads. Use Claude Fable 5.1 for demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work, or when your evals on Claude Opus 5.5 at higher effort still fall short." Same rule, with Opus 5.5 in place of Opus 5. Opus 5 is now listed as a legacy model.

That's a shift from how Fable 5 was positioned at its June launch, as the default top-tier pick. If you're choosing between the two today, that's the actual decision criterion Anthropic wants you using, not "which model is newer." Our Claude Opus 5.5 release breakdown covers what changed in 5.5, and our Claude Fable 5 pricing guide compares Fable 5.1 costs with Opus 5.5. We break down the full pricing and use-case tradeoff in Fable 5 vs Opus 4.8 and Opus 5 vs Fable 5 if you want the side-by-side.
5. Humanity's Last Exam rose from 57.8% to 60.9%

This is the no-tools reasoning benchmark, a 3.1-point gain. It's a smaller jump than the science benchmark but a meaningful one on a test that's specifically designed to resist memorization and reward genuine reasoning depth.
6. CursorBench rose from 70.5% to 73.4%

A 2.9-point gain on the coding-assistant benchmark version 3.2.0. Smallest of the six benchmark gains in the table above, but it's the one most directly relevant if your team uses Fable 5.1 or 5.1-based agents inside an IDE workflow rather than a pure terminal agent loop.

7. OSWorld 2.0 (partial) rose from 72.9% to 77.9%

A 5.0-point gain, larger than Humanity's Last Exam or CursorBench but well behind Terminal-Bench-Science, AutomationBench and Terminal-Bench 4.0. OSWorld tests an agent's ability to operate a real computer desktop environment: opening apps, navigating UI, completing multi-step tasks outside a sandboxed terminal. This is the benchmark most directly tied to computer-use agent work, which is the category behind a growing share of the AI agent development projects we scope for clients right now.
8. The named scientific and real-world results Anthropic cited at launch
Anthropic didn't just publish benchmark tables. It named specific outcomes:

Mythos 5.1 (not Fable 5.1) reached a hit rate of nearly 50% in protein binder design across 12 targets, and designed binders with 10 times higher affinity than competition submissions on three targets.
Venus surface mapping resolution improved from 10-20 kilometers to 2-3 kilometers.
Mythos 5.1 (again, not Fable 5.1) sped up seven deep learning models by up to 2.5 times and cut estimated GPU costs by 30-60% on genome-wide analyses.

Millennium, an investment firm, reported that Fable 5.1 identified the root cause of a rare system crash that its own engineers and other models had failed to solve over several years (reported by 9to5mac, Zac Hall, Sep 1 2026).

These are Anthropic's and third-party reported figures, not independently reproduced by us, and we're citing them as claims rather than facts we've verified ourselves. The protein and GPU results come from Mythos 5.1, so they show what the 5.1 generation can do rather than what Fable 5.1 does. They still matter more to a research team than any single percentage point on a leaderboard.
Should you switch from Fable 5 to Fable 5.1?

If you're already on Fable 5 through the API, AWS Bedrock, Google Cloud, or Microsoft Foundry, the practical answer is: switch the API identifier to claude-fable-5-1 and re-run your evals. Nothing about integration changed, context window, max output, and base pricing are identical, so this isn't a migration, it's a model swap.
Where it's worth checking your evals specifically:
Agentic workflows with repeated context: the cache pricing cut alone can justify the switch on cost grounds before you even factor in the accuracy gains.
Scientific or research coding tasks: the Terminal-Bench-Science jump is large enough that it's worth a direct A/B on your own task set, not just trusting the aggregate number.
Computer-use agents: the OSWorld gain (+5.0 points) is smaller than the Terminal-Bench 4.0 and AutomationBench gains, but relevant if your agents interact with real UIs rather than terminals or APIs.

General reasoning or coding where Opus 5.5 already clears your bar: per Anthropic's own guidance, don't default to Fable 5.1 here. Test Opus 5.5 at higher effort first. It costs $4/$20 per MTok against Fable 5.1's $10/$50, and its cache reads ($0.20/MTok) are now cheaper than Fable 5.1's ($0.25/MTok), so the cache cut in item #1 no longer gives Fable 5.1 a cost edge over Opus 5.5.

Not on Fable 5 yet? Then the question is Opus 5.5 or Fable 5.1, not Fable 5 or Fable 5.1. Start on Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) and move to Fable 5.1 only for the workloads where your evals show Opus 5.5 falling short. If you're on Opus 5 today, note that Anthropic lists four breaking changes in Opus 5.5, so moving is a small migration rather than a pure ID swap. Prices checked September 26, 2026 against Anthropic's pricing page.

If you're weighing Fable 5.1 against non-Anthropic alternatives entirely, our Fable 5 alternatives roundup still covers the field accurately. The pricing and benchmark deltas in this post add to that comparison, they don't replace it.

FAQ

What's new in Claude Fable 5.1 compared to Fable 5? Cache read pricing dropped 75% (from $1.00/MTok to $0.25/MTok), six benchmarks in Anthropic's comparison table improved (most notably Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, which more than doubled from 24.7% to 52.6%), and Anthropic released a restricted-access sibling model, Mythos 5.1. Context window, max output, and base input/output pricing are unchanged.

Is Claude Fable 5.1 more expensive than Fable 5? No. Base input ($10/MTok) and output ($50/MTok) pricing are identical. The only pricing change is cache reads, which got 75% cheaper. Anthropic states this makes typical workloads about 25% cheaper overall and highly agentic workloads up to about 45% cheaper.

What is Claude Mythos 5.1? The same underlying model as Fable 5.1, released with restricted access instead of Fable 5.1's standard safeguards. Access requires vetting through Anthropic's Cyber Verification Program (cybersecurity organizations) or Life Sciences Verification Program (life-sciences organizations), which Anthropic says was developed in partnership with the US government.

Should I use Fable 5.1 or Opus 5.5? Per Anthropic's models overview as of September 26, 2026, Opus 5.5 is the starting point for most workloads at $4/$20 per MTok. Reserve Fable 5.1 ($10/$50) for demanding reasoning or long-horizon agentic work, or cases where Opus 5.5 at higher effort still falls short on your evals. See our Opus 5.5 release breakdown and Opus 5 vs Fable 5 comparison.
What is Claude Fable 5.1's context window? Claude Fable 5.1 has a 1,048,576-token (1M) context window and a 128,000-token max output, both unchanged from Fable 5, per Anthropic's model overview.

Where can I access Claude Fable 5.1? Claude Code, the Claude Platform (Enterprise), the API (identifier claude-fable-5-1), AWS Bedrock, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry. Full setup steps are in how to access Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5.
What's the knowledge cutoff for Claude Fable 5.1? June 2026, per Anthropic's model overview docs. Anthropic states it won't retire the model sooner than September 1, 2027.

Is Mythos 5.1 better than Fable 5.1 at coding? On Terminal-Bench 4.0 specifically, yes: Mythos 5.1 scored 60.9% against Fable 5.1's 55.8% in Anthropic's own comparison table. Mythos 5.1 isn't generally available, though, so this only matters if you already qualify for restricted access.
